#!/usr/bin/env bash
# core/orch/contract.sh — Orchestrator backend contract layer (ADR-011, issue #219)
#
# Defines the orchestrator backend interface contract.  Strategy plugins
# (issues #198/#199/#200) source this file and provide implementations of
# the five contract functions.  The contract layer itself provides:
#
#   orch_has_capability <cap>   — queries the loaded backend's capabilities
#   orch_load_backend   <alias> — finds and sources a backend plugin by alias
#
# On file load, _orch_load_backend is called automatically to wire up the
# configured backend.  If no plugin is found, no-op stubs remain in place so
# callers can detect the "not implemented" state gracefully.
#
# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail settings; do not add set -euo pipefail here.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_CONTRACT_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_ORCH_CONTRACT_LOADED=1

# Sentinel: 0 = only stubs loaded, 1 = a real backend plugin was sourced.
# If any contract function is already defined when this file is sourced, a
# backend was pre-loaded (sourced before this contract file).  Mark it loaded
# so _orch_load_backend does not overwrite those implementations.
if declare -F orch_spawn >/dev/null 2>&1 || \
   declare -F orch_dispatch >/dev/null 2>&1 || \
   declare -F orch_capabilities >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
else
    _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=0
fi

_ZBUILD_ORCH_DIR="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)"
_ZBUILD_ROOT="$(cd "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_DIR}/../.." && pwd)"

# ─── Scratch directory for pool state ───────────────────────────────────────
# #898: the default is computed at use-time in `_strategy_orch_scratch_dir`
# (core/pipeline/strategies/common.sh) so it can be re-rooted under the per-run
# state dir (~/.zbuild/state/runs/<run_id>/orch) once ZBUILD_RUN_ID is known —
# the orchestrator analog of #887/#889. An explicit ZBUILD_ORCH_SCRATCH still
# overrides. (Was: a flat ~/.zbuild/state/orch baked here at source time, before
# run_id existed, which made per-run isolation impossible.)

# ─── _orch_not_implemented ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Emits an event and returns 1. Used by contract stubs before a backend loads.
_orch_not_implemented() {
    local fn_name="$1"
    local context="${2:-(no pool)}"
    # Emit event if emit_event is available (event-bus may not be loaded yet)
    if declare -F emit_event >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        emit_event "orch.contract.not_implemented" "fn=${fn_name}" "context=${context}" || true
    fi
    warn "orch contract: ${fn_name} not implemented (context: ${context})" || true
    return 1
}

# ─── Contract stubs — overridden by backend source ──────────────────────────
# These are only defined if the backend has not already provided them.

if ! declare -F orch_spawn >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    orch_spawn()        { _orch_not_implemented "orch_spawn" "$1"; }
fi

if ! declare -F orch_dispatch >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    orch_dispatch()     { _orch_not_implemented "orch_dispatch" "$1"; }
fi

if ! declare -F orch_collect >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    # Exit code convention: 0 = all passed; 1 otherwise, with
    # _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME = partial (some passed) | failed (#1850, ADR-054 §4:
    # partial was rc 2). Backends normalise work-unit exit codes — any non-zero
    # counts as fail; the original work-unit rc is NOT passed through.
    orch_collect()      { _orch_not_implemented "orch_collect" "$1"; }
fi

if ! declare -F orch_shutdown >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    orch_shutdown()     { _orch_not_implemented "orch_shutdown" "$1"; }
fi

if ! declare -F orch_capabilities >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    orch_capabilities() { _orch_not_implemented "orch_capabilities" "(no pool)"; }
fi

# ─── orch_has_capability ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Queries the loaded backend's capability list.
# Usage: orch_has_capability <capability_name>
# Returns 0 if the capability is present in orch_capabilities output, 1 if not.
orch_has_capability() {
    local cap="$1"
    local caps
    caps="$(orch_capabilities 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
    if grep -qF "\"${cap}\"" <<< "$caps"; then
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

# ─── _orch_find_backend_dir ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Lightweight backend plugin discovery that does NOT require the full registry.
# Scans $plugins_root for a plugin whose manifest declares:
#   provides.role: orchestrator-backend
#   AND (id: <alias> OR provides.alias: <alias>)
# Prints the plugin directory on success.  Returns 1 if not found.
_orch_find_backend_dir() {
    local alias="$1"
    local plugins_root="${2:-${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT:-${_ZBUILD_ROOT}/plugins}}"

    [[ -d "$plugins_root" ]] || return 1

    local manifest plugin_dir
    while IFS= read -r manifest; do
        plugin_dir="$(dirname "$manifest")"
        # Check provides.role
        if ! grep -q 'role:.*orchestrator-backend' "$manifest" 2>/dev/null; then
            continue
        fi
        # Check id or provides.alias match
        local id declared_alias
        id="$(awk '/^id:/ { sub(/^id:[[:space:]]*/, ""); print; exit }' "$manifest" 2>/dev/null)"
        declared_alias="$(awk '/^[[:space:]]*alias:/ { sub(/^[[:space:]]*alias:[[:space:]]*/, ""); print; exit }' "$manifest" 2>/dev/null)"
        if [[ "$id" == "$alias" || "$declared_alias" == "$alias" ]]; then
            echo "$plugin_dir"
            return 0
        fi
    done < <(find "$plugins_root" -maxdepth 4 -name 'manifest.yaml' -type f 2>/dev/null)

    return 1
}

# ─── orch_load_backend ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Finds and sources a backend plugin by its alias.
# Usage: orch_load_backend <alias>
# Uses find_plugin_for_role (if available) or lightweight _orch_find_backend_dir
# to locate the plugin, then sources plugin.sh.
# Falls back to the built-in orch-sequential plugin if the alias is "sequential".
# If no plugin is found, emits a warning and returns 1.
orch_load_backend() {
    local backend="${1:-}"
    local plugin_dir

    if [[ -z "$backend" ]]; then
        warn "orch_load_backend: no backend alias provided" || true
        return 1
    fi

    # Try registry lookup if find_plugin_for_role is available
    if declare -F find_plugin_for_role >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        plugin_dir="$(find_plugin_for_role "orchestrator-backend" "$backend" 2>/dev/null)" || plugin_dir=""
        if [[ -n "$plugin_dir" && -f "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
            # shellcheck disable=SC1090
            source "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh"
            _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
            return 0
        fi
    fi

    # Fallback: lightweight scan without the full registry
    plugin_dir="$(_orch_find_backend_dir "$backend" 2>/dev/null)" || plugin_dir=""
    if [[ -n "$plugin_dir" && -f "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
        # shellcheck disable=SC1090
        source "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh"
        _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
        return 0
    fi

    # Fallback: try built-in orch-sequential plugin by known path
    local sequential_sh="${_ZBUILD_ROOT}/plugins/tool/orch-sequential/plugin.sh"
    if [[ "$backend" == "sequential" && -f "$sequential_sh" ]]; then
        # shellcheck disable=SC1090
        source "$sequential_sh"
        _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
        return 0
    fi

    # No plugin found for requested backend — fall back to sequential (built-in)
    if [[ -f "$sequential_sh" ]]; then
        warn "orch_load_backend: backend '${backend}' not found; falling back to sequential" || true
        # shellcheck disable=SC1090
        source "$sequential_sh"
        _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
        return 0
    fi

    # Nothing found at all — warn and return 1
    warn "orch_load_backend: backend '${backend}' not found (no plugin for role orchestrator-backend with alias ${backend})" || true
    return 1
}

# ─── _orch_load_backend (internal) ───────────────────────────────────────────
# Called at end of file to auto-load the configured backend.
# Skips auto-loading if a backend has already provided the contract functions
# (i.e., when a plugin sources the backend before sourcing this contract file).
_orch_load_backend() {
    # If a real backend was already sourced (sentinel set to 1), skip auto-load
    # to avoid overwriting the pre-loaded backend's implementations.
    # Note: the stubs above do NOT set this sentinel, so checking declare -F
    # would always return true (stubs are defined).  We use the sentinel instead.
    [[ "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED:-0}" -eq 1 ]] && return 0

    local backend

    # Get configured backend, falling back to "sequential" if config unavailable
    if declare -F zbuild_config_get_backend >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        backend="$(zbuild_config_get_backend "orchestrator" 2>/dev/null)" || backend="sequential"
    else
        backend="${ZBUILD_ORCHESTRATOR_BACKEND:-sequential}"
    fi

    # Attempt to load the configured backend; if it fails, that is OK —
    # the stubs remain and callers will get informative errors.
    orch_load_backend "$backend" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# Auto-load at source time — skipped if _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED is already 1
_orch_load_backend

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# core/orch/local_engine.sh — shared dispatch/collect/poll/shutdown for the
# local-execution orchestrator backends (orch-bash-parallel, orch-ruflo-hive).
# Extracted from those two plugins in #281 because they had ~80% duplication
# and the #269 normaliser fix had to be applied twice (and still missed
# orch-mock — caught belatedly in #278). Single source of truth now.
#
# Pool layout (caller chooses prefix + pid subdir name):
#   <pool_dir>/<pid_subdir>/<slot>.pid       — wrapper subshell PID
#   <pool_dir>/results/<slot>.{stdout,stderr,exit,inner_pid}
#
# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail; no set -euo pipefail.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_ENGINE_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_ENGINE_LOADED=1

_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_DIR="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)"
_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_ROOT="$(cd "$_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# Defensive source: warn (scripts/lib/helpers.sh).
if ! declare -F warn >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    source "$_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
fi

# _orch_local_make_slot_id — collision-resistant slot id (epoch-ns + PID + rand)
_orch_local_make_slot_id() {
    date +%s%N
    printf -- '-%s-' "$$"
    openssl rand -hex 8 2>/dev/null || printf '%05d%05d%05d' $RANDOM $RANDOM $RANDOM
}

# _orch_local_kill_slot <sig> <wrapper_pid> [inner_pid]
# Sends signal to both the wrapper PID and the inner work-unit PID (if known).
_orch_local_kill_slot() {
    local sig="$1"
    local wrapper_pid="$2"
    local inner_pid="${3:-}"
    kill "-${sig}" "$wrapper_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
    [[ -n "$inner_pid" ]] && kill "-${sig}" "$inner_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# _orch_local_dispatch_workunit <pool_dir> <pid_subdir> <work_unit> <caller_tag>
# Dispatches <work_unit> (must be an executable file path) in a background
# subshell. Records wrapper PID and inner PID; installs trap to propagate
# SIGTERM/EXIT to the inner process.
#
# Output: prints slot_id to stdout AND sets the global _ORCH_LOCAL_LAST_SLOT_ID.
# Callers needing the slot_id after dispatch (e.g. for downstream telemetry)
# MUST read the global, NOT use command substitution: `$(_orch_local_dispatch_workunit ...)`
# forks a subshell whose EXIT trap (installed by test-helpers.sh or similar)
# `pkill -P $$`s the wrapper subshell we just spawned. The global pattern
# avoids that subshell entirely. (Caught in #282 second-round review.)
#
# Returns 0 on successful dispatch, 1 on validation/permission failure.
_orch_local_dispatch_workunit() {
    local pool_dir="$1"
    local pid_subdir="$2"
    local work_unit="$3"
    local caller_tag="${4:-orch_local}"

    _ORCH_LOCAL_LAST_SLOT_ID=""

    if [[ ! -f "$work_unit" || ! -x "$work_unit" ]]; then
        warn "${caller_tag}: work_unit must be a path to an executable file: ${work_unit}" || true
        return 1
    fi

    # Ensure pool dirs exist even if the caller skipped pre-spawn.
    mkdir -p "${pool_dir}/results" "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}" 2>/dev/null || {
        warn "${caller_tag}: pool dir is not writable: ${pool_dir}" || true
        return 1
    }

    local slot_id
    slot_id="$(_orch_local_make_slot_id | tr -d '\n')"
    local result_base="${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}"

    # Background subshell: writes inner work-unit PID, traps on exit to
    # propagate signals, then waits for inner and writes .exit file.
    (
        local rc=0 inner=0
        # #2108: dispatched from a `<<< "$roles_out"` loop — never its stdin.
        bash "$work_unit" </dev/null > "${result_base}.stdout" 2> "${result_base}.stderr" &
        inner=$!
        echo "$inner" > "${result_base}.inner_pid"
        trap 'kill -KILL "$inner" 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT INT TERM
        wait "$inner" || rc=$?
        trap - EXIT INT TERM
        echo "$rc" > "${result_base}.exit"
    ) &
    local worker_pid=$!
    echo "$worker_pid" > "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}/${slot_id}.pid"
    _ORCH_LOCAL_LAST_SLOT_ID="$slot_id"
    echo "$slot_id"
    return 0
}

# _orch_local_collect_results <pool_dir> <pid_subdir> <timeout_s>
# Polls .exit files for every slot in <pool_dir>/<pid_subdir>/; streams
# stdout/stderr. Returns the normalised orch contract code:
#   0 = all dispatched work units exited 0  (pool dir removed)
#   1 = otherwise (pool dir preserved); _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME says which —
#       `failed` (all exited non-zero) or `partial` (at least one passed).
#       #1850 (ADR-054 §4): `partial` used to be rc 2.
# Work-unit exit codes are normalised — original rc is not passed through.
# Single source of truth for the normaliser (#269 + #278 + #281).
_orch_local_collect_results() {
    local pool_dir="$1"
    local pid_subdir="$2"
    local timeout_s="${3:-0}"
    _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="failed"

    [[ -d "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}" ]] || { _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="passed"; return 0; }

    local pass_count=0 fail_count=0
    local deadline=0
    [[ "$timeout_s" -gt 0 ]] && deadline=$(( ${EPOCHSECONDS:-$(date +%s)} + timeout_s ))

    local pid_file slot_id result_base wrapper_pid inner_pid rc
    for pid_file in "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}/"*.pid; do
        [[ -f "$pid_file" ]] || continue
        slot_id="$(basename "${pid_file%.pid}")"
        result_base="${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}"
        wrapper_pid="$(cat "$pid_file")"
        inner_pid=""
        [[ -f "${result_base}.inner_pid" ]] && inner_pid="$(cat "${result_base}.inner_pid")"

        while [[ ! -f "${result_base}.exit" ]]; do
            if [[ "$timeout_s" -gt 0 && "${EPOCHSECONDS:-$(date +%s)}" -ge "$deadline" ]]; then
                _orch_local_kill_slot TERM "$wrapper_pid" "$inner_pid"
                sleep 0.5
                _orch_local_kill_slot KILL "$wrapper_pid" "$inner_pid"
                echo "124" > "${result_base}.exit"
                break
            fi
            sleep 0.1  # fork-budget-exempt: polls until the slot exits — the count is how long it ran (#2236)
        done

        rc="$(cat "${result_base}.exit" 2>/dev/null || echo 1)"
        [[ -f "${result_base}.stdout" ]] && cat "${result_base}.stdout"
        [[ -f "${result_base}.stderr" ]] && cat "${result_base}.stderr" >&2
        if [[ "$rc" -eq 0 ]]; then
            pass_count=$((pass_count + 1))
        else
            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
        fi
    done

    if [[ "$fail_count" -eq 0 ]]; then
        rm -rf "$pool_dir"
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="passed"
        return 0
    elif [[ "$pass_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="partial"
        return 1
    else
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="failed"
        return 1
    fi
}

# _orch_local_shutdown_pool <pool_dir> <pid_subdir>
# Best-effort SIGTERM → 0.5s → SIGKILL on every slot, then rm -rf the pool dir.
# Idempotent — safe to call on non-existent pools.
_orch_local_shutdown_pool() {
    local pool_dir="$1"
    local pid_subdir="$2"

    [[ -d "$pool_dir" ]] || return 0

    local pid_file slot_id wrapper_pid inner_pid
    for pid_file in "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}/"*.pid; do
        [[ -f "$pid_file" ]] || continue
        slot_id="$(basename "${pid_file%.pid}")"
        wrapper_pid="$(cat "$pid_file")"
        inner_pid=""
        [[ -f "${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}.inner_pid" ]] && \
            inner_pid="$(cat "${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}.inner_pid")"
        _orch_local_kill_slot TERM "$wrapper_pid" "$inner_pid"
    done
    sleep 0.5
    for pid_file in "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}/"*.pid; do
        [[ -f "$pid_file" ]] || continue
        slot_id="$(basename "${pid_file%.pid}")"
        wrapper_pid="$(cat "$pid_file")"
        inner_pid=""
        [[ -f "${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}.inner_pid" ]] && \
            inner_pid="$(cat "${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}.inner_pid")"
        _orch_local_kill_slot KILL "$wrapper_pid" "$inner_pid"
    done
    rm -rf "$pool_dir"
    return 0
}

2	# scripts/lib/proc-group.sh — process-group resolution and kill helpers.
3	# Extracted from core/router/route.sh (Wave 15-G, #687) so the test stage and
4	# any other long-running spawn share one implementation (#1748).
5	# Sourced library: no set -euo pipefail.
6	
7	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_PROC_GROUP_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
8	_ZBUILD_PROC_GROUP_LOADED=1
9	
10	# #2056: there is no setsid prefix any more. Process groups come from `set -m`
11	# at the spawn site — bash job control makes a backgrounded job a group leader,
12	# which is POSIX and identical on macOS and Linux.
13	#
14	# `setsid -w` was wrong here twice over. It is absent on macOS (util-linux is
15	# keg-only), so the prefix went empty, no group was created, and an abort
16	# degraded to a single-PID kill while every descendant survived — the Wave 15-G
17	# guarantee held on Linux only, and the test covering it is Linux-only too, so
18	# nothing said so. And `-w` forces setsid to fork, because it waits for the
19	# child and returns its exit status, so the pid the caller captured was the
20	# wrapper rather than the new session leader.
21	#
22	# Do not reintroduce a prefix here. A spawn that needs an external binary to get
23	# a process group is a spawn whose guarantee is platform-conditional.
24	
25	# Prints the PGID safe to signal for <pid>, or nothing. Empty is not "no group":
26	# it means the group could not be proven distinct from ours, and signalling it
27	# would take down the runner itself — so callers must fall back to a PID kill.
28	zbuild_pg_resolve() {
29	    local _pid="${1:-}"
30	    [[ -n "$_pid" && "$_pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
31	    local _child _self
32	    _child="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$_pid" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
33	    _self="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
34	    if [[ -n "$_child" && -n "$_self" && "$_child" != "$_self" ]]; then
35	        printf '%s' "$_child"
36	        return 0
37	    fi
38	    # A short-lived child can exit before `ps` reports it. Under `set -m` the
39	    # spawn IS the group leader, so PGID == PID by construction and that stays
40	    # true after it is gone — reporting the pid is correct, not a guess.
41	    #
42	    # This branch previously justified itself with "setsid execs in place, so it
43	    # needs no fork". That was false under `-w` (#2056): setsid forks in order to
44	    # wait, so the captured pid was the wrapper and the group belonged to a
45	    # process one fork below. Under job control there is no wrapper to be wrong
46	    # about.
47	    if [[ -z "$_child" ]]; then
48	        printf '%s' "$_pid"
49	    fi
50	}
51	
52	# TERM <target>, then KILL whatever is left after <grace_s>. Shared by the group

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/lib/proc-group.sh — process-group resolution and kill helpers.
# Extracted from core/router/route.sh (Wave 15-G, #687) so the test stage and
# any other long-running spawn share one implementation (#1748).
# Sourced library: no set -euo pipefail.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_PROC_GROUP_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_PROC_GROUP_LOADED=1

# #2056: there is no setsid prefix any more. Process groups come from `set -m`
# at the spawn site — bash job control makes a backgrounded job a group leader,
# which is POSIX and identical on macOS and Linux.
#
# `setsid -w` was wrong here twice over. It is absent on macOS (util-linux is
# keg-only), so the prefix went empty, no group was created, and an abort
# degraded to a single-PID kill while every descendant survived — the Wave 15-G
# guarantee held on Linux only, and the test covering it is Linux-only too, so
# nothing said so. And `-w` forces setsid to fork, because it waits for the
# child and returns its exit status, so the pid the caller captured was the
# wrapper rather than the new session leader.
#
# Do not reintroduce a prefix here. A spawn that needs an external binary to get
# a process group is a spawn whose guarantee is platform-conditional.

# Prints the PGID safe to signal for <pid>, or nothing. Empty is not "no group":
# it means the group could not be proven distinct from ours, and signalling it
# would take down the runner itself — so callers must fall back to a PID kill.
zbuild_pg_resolve() {
    local _pid="${1:-}"
    [[ -n "$_pid" && "$_pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
    local _child _self
    _child="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$_pid" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
    _self="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
    if [[ -n "$_child" && -n "$_self" && "$_child" != "$_self" ]]; then
        printf '%s' "$_child"
        return 0
    fi
    # A short-lived child can exit before `ps` reports it. Under `set -m` the
    # spawn IS the group leader, so PGID == PID by construction and that stays
    # true after it is gone — reporting the pid is correct, not a guess.
    #
    # This branch previously justified itself with "setsid execs in place, so it
    # needs no fork". That was false under `-w` (#2056): setsid forks in order to
    # wait, so the captured pid was the wrapper and the group belonged to a
    # process one fork below. Under job control there is no wrapper to be wrong
    # about.
    if [[ -z "$_child" ]]; then
        printf '%s' "$_pid"
    fi
}

# TERM <target>, then KILL whatever is left after <grace_s>. Shared by the group
# and single-PID paths so both get the same grace — the escalation is the whole
# contract, and a caller that skips it is indistinguishable from a plain KILL.
#
# Synchronous by construction (#905): the `{ sleep 1 && kill -KILL; } &` backstop
# this replaces could outlive the caller that armed it, so teardown returned
# while the tree was still alive and the backstop was sometimes lost with it.
# Polling instead costs milliseconds when the target exits on TERM, costs the
# full grace only when it ignores TERM, and leaves nothing running on return.
_zbuild_pg_term_then_kill() {
    # `--` because a group target is spelled `-PGID` and would otherwise parse
    # as an option.
    local _target="$1" _grace="$2"
    kill -TERM -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || true
    local _ticks=$(( _grace * 10 )) _i=0
    while (( _i < _ticks )); do
        kill -0 -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || return 0
        sleep 0.1 2>/dev/null || true
        _i=$(( _i + 1 ))
    done
    kill -KILL -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# A non-numeric grace would evaluate to 0 in the arithmetic context above, so the
# poll loop would never run and the target would go straight to KILL — silently
# losing the escalation the caller asked for. Clamp to the default instead.
_zbuild_pg_grace() {
    local _g="${1:-1}"
    [[ "$_g" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_g" -gt 0 ]] && printf '%s' "$_g" || printf '1'
}

# zbuild_pg_record_pgid <file> — the pgid out of a `.pgid` record.
#
# ONE reader, because there are two formats on disk and three places that read
# them (#2018). The engine's dispatch record is `<pgid>\t<leader start time>`;
# tool/test's own `test-stage.pgid` is a bare number; and a record written before
# #2018 is bare too. A reader that only understands one of those does not error —
# it fails the numeric guard and `continue`s, so the caller kills NOTHING and
# reports success. That is how a format change here silently disables ADR-062 §2
# reclamation, which is the path that actually runs on every normal exit.
#
# Prints nothing and returns 1 when there is no usable pgid, so a caller can
# still distinguish "no record" from "record says 1234".
zbuild_pg_record_pgid() {
    local _f="${1:-}" _pgid=""
    [[ -n "$_f" && -f "$_f" ]] || return 1
    IFS=$'\t' read -r _pgid _ 2>/dev/null < "$_f" || true
    [[ "$_pgid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 1
    printf '%s' "$_pgid"
}

# zbuild_pg_register <pgid> — record a process group the caller just created.
#
# ADR-062 §1 had the ENGINE record this at dispatch. It could not, and the reason
# is structural: a stage is a bash function call, not a subprocess, so at the
# dispatch seam no group exists yet. That code fell back to `$$`'s group — the
# engine's own — which teardown then skipped, correctly, because signalling your
# own group takes the runner down with it. Every record was unkillable, every
# record was skipped, and §2's kill loop never freed anything (#2024).
#
# So the direction reverses: whoever CREATES a group registers it. Two sites do,
# and only two — `tool/test`'s `set -m` suite and the router's `setsid` spawn.
#
# Refusing to register our own group is the invariant, not a safety check. A
# record naming the registrar's own group is strictly worse than no record: it
# cannot be acted on, and it makes the mechanism look live while it does nothing
# — which is exactly how the original defect survived #2001, #2018 and an ADR.
#
# Fail-open throughout: a spawn is never refused because bookkeeping was
# unavailable. Silence here costs a possible leak; failing here costs the run.
zbuild_pg_register() {
    local _pgid="${1:-}"
    [[ -n "$_pgid" && "$_pgid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
    local _self
    _self="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
    [[ -n "$_self" && "$_self" == "$_pgid" ]] && return 0
    local _sd="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}"
    [[ -n "$_sd" && -d "$_sd" ]] || return 0
    local _stage="${2:-${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}}"
    [[ -n "$_stage" ]] || return 0
    # One path component, sanitised the same way stage scratch keys are, so no
    # stage name can climb out of runtime/.
    _stage="${_stage//[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/_}"
    local _dir="${_sd}/runtime/stages"
    mkdir -p "$_dir" 2>/dev/null || return 0
    # #2018 format: the leader's start time proves the pgid still names what
    # recorded it, so a later sweep cannot signal a recycled pid.
    local _start
    _start="$(ps -o lstart= -p "$_pgid" 2>/dev/null | tr -s ' ' | sed 's/^ *//;s/ *$//' || true)"
    printf '%s\t%s' "$_pgid" "$_start" > "${_dir}/${_stage}.pgid" 2>/dev/null || true
    return 0
}

# TERM then KILL a whole process group. `-PGID` is the negative-pid convention.
zbuild_pg_kill() {
    local _pgid="${1:-}"
    [[ -n "$_pgid" && "$_pgid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
    # Refuse our own group: `kill -- -PGID` from inside it takes down the runner.
    local _self
    _self="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
    [[ -n "$_self" && "$_self" == "$_pgid" ]] && return 0
    _zbuild_pg_term_then_kill "-$_pgid" "$(_zbuild_pg_grace "${2:-}")"
}

# TERM then KILL a single PID — the path taken when no group could be proven.
# It gets the same grace as the group path: a suite that flushes coverage or
# writes partial results on SIGTERM needs the window wherever it is killed from.
zbuild_pid_kill() {
    local _pid="${1:-}"
    [[ -n "$_pid" && "$_pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
    _zbuild_pg_term_then_kill "$_pid" "$(_zbuild_pg_grace "${2:-}")"
}

151	_RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON=""
152	
153	# ─── _runner_retry_budget <stage> (#2187, was #1887's redispatch budget) ─────
154	# How many times a stage whose disposition says `retry` is re-dispatched. The
155	# word never carries a count: the template's per-stage `retry:` wins, then the
156	# ZBUILD_DISPOSITION_REDISPATCH knob, then the engine default 3. Capped at 5 —
157	# the cycle re-runs its members anyway, so this is not a budget for grinding.
158	# A value above the cap clamps to the cap; a non-number is ignored.
159	_runner_retry_budget() {
160	    local v=""
161	    if declare -F template_stage_retry >/dev/null 2>&1; then
162	        v="$(template_stage_retry "${1:-}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
163	    fi
164	    [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || v="${ZBUILD_DISPOSITION_REDISPATCH:-}"
165	    [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || v=3
166	    (( v > 5 )) && v=5
167	    printf '%s' "$v"
168	}

170	# ─── _runner_leaf_contract_halt <state_file> <stage> <reason> ───────────────
171	# A leaf stage whose v2 result the engine rejected ends the run; rc 0 when it
172	# did. A cycle already halts on this (#550); a leaf recorded `error` and went on,
173	# which is how #1835's run shipped a plan result with no `reason`. Safe ahead of
174	# #1798: a contract violation is a zBuild defect (ADR-054 §6 `broken`), never a
175	# transient failure, so this cannot turn a network hiccup into a dead run.
176	# Reads main()'s _runner_run_id / _runner_issue and sets its _runner_ended.
177	_runner_leaf_contract_halt() {
178	    local sf="$1" st="$2" why="${3:-}"
179	    [[ "$why" == contract_violation:* ]] || return 1
180	    _update_stage_status "$sf" "$st" "failed"
181	    _set_pipeline_status "$sf" "failed"
182	    eb_emit_event "stage.fail" "stage=$st" "reason=$why" 2>/dev/null || true
183	    eb_emit_event "pipeline.end" "status=failed" "stage=$st" "reason=$why" \
184	        "run_id=${_runner_run_id:-}" "issue=${_runner_issue:-}" 2>/dev/null || true
185	    _render_pipeline_end "failed" "$st"
186	    _runner_ended=true
187	    error "Stage $st wrote a result the engine rejects ($why) — a zBuild defect; the run stops here"
188	    return 0
189	}

191	# ─── _runner_leaf_verdict_halt <state_file> <stage> <class> <raw> ────────────
192	# #1798 (ADR-054 §4): a leaf stage that reports a failure ends the run; rc 0
193	# when it did. <class> is the classified verdict the runner already read
194	# (runner_read_stage_verdict: fail, or a structural word passed through);
195	# <raw> is the stage's own word, which the run's end names. A cycle acts on its
196	# members' verdicts; a leaf used to record one, pick a glyph from it and
197	# complete anyway. A template opts a stage out with `blocking: false`
198	# (ADR-013) — advisory by declaration, never by accident.
199	_runner_leaf_verdict_halt() {
200	    local sf="$1" st="$2" v="${3:-}" raw="${4:-}"
201	    case "$v" in
202	        fail|error|block|scope_violation|corrupt_diff) ;;
203	        *) return 1 ;;
204	    esac
205	    [[ "$(template_stage_blocking "$st" 2>/dev/null)" == "false" ]] && return 1
206	    [[ -n "$raw" && "$raw" != "missing" ]] || raw="$v"
207	    _update_stage_status "$sf" "$st" "failed"
208	    _zbuild_state_set_stage_verdict "$sf" "$st" "$v"
209	    _set_pipeline_status "$sf" "failed"
210	    # No `rc=` field: the stage exited 0, so a verdict-triggered stage.fail
211	    # carries the stage's word (`verdict=`) instead — as the contract halt
212	    # carries `reason=` alone. A consumer of stage.fail reads either shape.
213	    eb_emit_event "stage.fail" "stage=$st" "verdict=$raw" "reason=stage_failed:$raw" 2>/dev/null || true
214	    eb_emit_event "pipeline.end" "status=failed" "stage=$st" "reason=stage_failed:$raw" \
215	        "run_id=${_runner_run_id:-}" "issue=${_runner_issue:-}" 2>/dev/null || true
216	    _render_pipeline_end "failed" "$st"
217	    _runner_ended=true
218	    error "Stage $st reported $raw — the run stops here"
219	    return 0
220	}

222	# ─── _runner_attempt_made_progress <artifact_dir> <stage> <iter> (#2187) ─────
223	# Attempts are numbered from 1 (attempt-archive.sh writes n+1).
224	# rc 0 when the stage's LATEST attempt in this iteration changed any of its
225	# declared outputs (the #2186 attempt record), or when there is no record to
226	# judge by; rc 1 when every output it recorded came back unchanged or absent —
227	# retrying the same work would hit the same wall.
228	_runner_attempt_made_progress() {
229	    local base="${1:-}/attempts/${2//[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/_}" iter="${3:-0}"
230	    [[ -d "$base" ]] || return 0
231	    local latest="" n=0 d k
232	    for d in "$base"/iter-"$iter"-attempt-*; do
233	        [[ -f "$d/attempt.json" ]] || continue
234	        k="${d##*-attempt-}"
235	        [[ "$k" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
236	        (( k > n )) && { n="$k"; latest="$d/attempt.json"; }
237	    done
238	    [[ -n "$latest" ]] || return 0
239	    # #2252: the archive's own judgement of the WORK, when it made one.
240	    if jq -e 'has("progress")' "$latest" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
241	        jq -e '.progress == true' "$latest" >/dev/null 2>&1
242	        return
243	    fi
244	    jq -e 'has("outputs") | not' "$latest" >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0
245	    jq -e '[.outputs[]] | any(. == "changed")' "$latest" >/dev/null 2>&1
246	}

248	# ─── _runner_note_push_failure <stage> (#2187) ───────────────────────────────
249	# Report a failed stage-end push once per distinct reason, on the same channel
250	# and dedupe as a failed snapshot.
251	_runner_note_push_failure() {
252	    [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" == "failed" ]] || return 0
253	    [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-}" != "${_RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON:-}" ]] || return 0
254	    _RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON="${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
255	    eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.failed" "stage=${1:-unknown}" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
256	        "reason=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}" 2>/dev/null || true
257	    warn "stage-end push failed at stage '${1:-unknown}': ${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
258	}

260	# ─── _runner_push_work_branch <state_dir> <stage> (#2187) ────────────────────
261	# When the run has a work branch on origin (ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH — CI sets
262	# zbuild/issue-N-ci), push the run's commits to it at every stage end, so a new
263	# session can pick them up even if this runner dies. No changes, no save: only
264	# when HEAD carries commits past the commit the run started from, which the
265	# engine sets before any stage (#2367; #1801 run 38290215955: the end of hydrate
266	# force-pushed main over the branch's earlier work). Advisory: a failure is
267	# reported, never fatal.
268	_runner_push_work_branch() {
269	    local _branch="${ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH:-}"
270	    [[ -n "$_branch" ]] || return 0
271	    local _repo="${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}"
272	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || _repo="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)"
273	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || return 0
274	    git -C "$_repo" remote get-url origin >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
275	    local _base="${ZBUILD_RUN_START_COMMIT:-}" _ahead
276	    [[ -n "$_base" ]] || return 0
277	    _ahead="$(git -C "$_repo" rev-list --count "$_base..HEAD" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
278	    [[ "$_ahead" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_ahead" -gt 0 ]] || return 0
279	    local _err
280	    if _err="$(git -C "$_repo" push --force -q origin "HEAD:refs/heads/$_branch" 2>&1)"; then
281	        return 0
282	    fi
283	    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
284	    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="git push work branch $_branch failed: $(tr '\n' ' ' <<< "$_err" | cut -c1-300)"
285	    _runner_note_push_failure "${2:-unknown}"
286	    return 0
287	}

289	# ─── _runner_keep_head_on_branch <state_dir> <stage> (#2264) ─────────────────
290	# A model call can leave HEAD off the run branch; every later commit then lands
291	# on HEAD alone while the branch ref — which pr-open checks out and the post-run
292	# step pushes — falls behind. #1844 run 37066147994 lost its work that way. At
293	# every stage end, put HEAD back on the branch when that drops nothing, and say
294	# which stage left it off; when the two diverged, move nothing and say so.
295	_runner_keep_head_on_branch() {
296	    local _stage="${2:-unknown}" _branch="${ZBUILD_RUN_BRANCH:-}"
297	    [[ -n "$_branch" ]] || return 0
298	    local _repo="${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}"
299	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || _repo="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)"
300	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || return 0
301	    zbuild_keep_head_on_branch "$_repo" "$_branch"
302	    case "$ZBUILD_HEAD_OUTCOME" in
303	        reattached)
304	            eb_emit_event "pipeline.head.reattached" "stage=$_stage" "branch=$_branch" \
305	                "was=$ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS" 2>/dev/null || true
306	            warn "stage '$_stage' left HEAD off the run branch ($ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS) — moved '$_branch' to HEAD" ;;
307	        diverged)
308	            eb_emit_event "pipeline.head.diverged" "stage=$_stage" "branch=$_branch" \
309	                "was=$ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS" 2>/dev/null || true
310	            warn "stage '$_stage' left HEAD off the run branch and the two diverged — '$_branch' not moved" ;;
311	    esac
312	    return 0
313	}

315	# ─── _runner_snapshot_artifacts <state_dir> <stage> (ADR-050, #1581/#1878) ───
316	# Snapshot the artifact area onto the state branch at a stage boundary, so a
317	# completed stage's work survives a mid-run crash/rate-limit and is available to
318	# the next run. Stage-agnostic (snapshots whatever files exist) and advisory —
319	# never blocks a run.
320	#
321	# #1878: ONE definition, called from every stage-completion site on the LIVE
322	# dispatch-unit path. It previously existed only inline in the legacy linear stage
323	# loop below — which no shipped template ever reaches (any cycle/map/parallel unit
324	# sets _run_dispatch_units=1, and every terminal branch of that block returns), so
325	# the snapshot was never invoked at all and the store was always empty. That is
326	# item 1 of #1807.
327	#
328	# #1878: also no longer swallows stderr. A snapshot that fails now says so, with
329	# the failing git operation named, instead of returning 1 into a `2>/dev/null`
330	# and leaving no trace anywhere.
331	_runner_snapshot_artifacts() {
332	    # $1 may be empty: the cycle-orchestrator call site is several frames from
333	    # main(), and relying on main()'s `state_dir` local reaching it through
334	    # dynamic scope is exactly the kind of implicit coupling that makes a call
335	    # site silently no-op. The runner exports the resolved per-run value at
336	    # runner.sh:1739, so fall back to that.
337	    local _snap_state_dir="${1:-}" _snap_stage="${2:-unknown}"
338	    [[ -n "$_snap_state_dir" ]] || _snap_state_dir="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}"
339	    [[ -n "$_snap_state_dir" ]] || return 0
340	    # Before the identity guard: a --goal or local run needs its branch kept too.
341	    _runner_keep_head_on_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
342	    # #1931: identity, not issue number. `issue > 0` excluded every --goal run
343	    # from the durable store, so nothing was ever snapshotted for one and the
344	    # push had nothing to send.
345	    _artifact_persist_has_identity "$_runner_issue" || return 0
346	
347	    _artifact_persist_snapshot "$_snap_state_dir" "$_runner_issue" || true
348	    case "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" in
349	        saved)
350	            eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.saved" \
351	                "stage=$_snap_stage" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
352	                "skipped=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_SKIPPED:-0}" 2>/dev/null || true
353	            ;;
354	        failed)
355	            # Loud, not fatal. This event is the whole point of #1878: the defect
356	            # went undiagnosed for the life of the feature because the failure had
357	            # no channel to surface on.
358	            #
359	            # Deduped on the reason. Most failures are a STATIC precondition — no
360	            # resolvable repository, a ref D/F conflict — so they recur identically
361	            # at every stage boundary. Reporting the first occurrence keeps the
362	            # signal; repeating it once per stage is noise that trains an operator
363	            # to ignore the event. A CHANGED reason is always reported.
364	            if [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-}" != "${_RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON:-}" ]]; then
365	                _RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON="${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
366	                eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.failed" \
367	                    "stage=$_snap_stage" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
368	                    "reason=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}" 2>/dev/null || true
369	                warn "artifact snapshot failed at stage '$_snap_stage': ${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
370	            fi
371	            ;;
372	        # empty / unchanged are not failures and are not events: emitting
373	        # `saved` for them is precisely the lie this change removes.
374	        *) : ;;
375	    esac
376	    # #2187: push at the stage end, not only when the run ends — a run killed
377	    # mid-way (job ceiling, SIGKILL) otherwise loses everything since its start.
378	    # Only for a run that declares where its work goes (ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH;
379	    # the CI pipeline sets it). A plain local run — and every test — pushes
380	    # nothing here: tests have left state branches in real checkouts, and
381	    # this would put them on origin. The persist stage still pushes at the end.
382	    [[ -n "${ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH:-}" ]] || return 0
383	    local _leak=""
384	    if _leak="$(_artifact_persist_find_secret "$_snap_state_dir/artifacts")"; then
385	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
386	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="refusing to push — artifact looks like it carries a credential (${_leak})"
387	        _runner_note_push_failure "$_snap_stage"
388	        # The scan covers the artifact area, not the working tree: the run's
389	        # code commits still go to the work branch.
390	        _runner_push_work_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
391	        return 0
392	    fi
393	    if [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" == "saved" ]]; then
394	        _artifact_persist_push "$_runner_issue" "${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}" || true
395	        _runner_note_push_failure "$_snap_stage"
396	    fi
397	    _runner_push_work_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
398	    return 0
399	}

401	# ─── stage-start time cache (#508) ───────────────────────────────────────────
402	# Populated immediately before _render_stage_divider for each stage; read at
403	# the ✓/✗ complete/fail sites to compute the duration suffix. assoc array so
404	# nested / out-of-order stages (none today, but safe) still resolve correctly.
405	declare -gA _RUNNER_STAGE_START_MS=()
406	
407	# ─── pipeline-wide start time cache (#525) ───────────────────────────────────
408	# Populated once at the top of main() right after _runner_run_id is sanitized
409	# (well before the EXIT trap installs) so every pipeline.end emit site — incl.
410	# preflight failure (L289) and the EXIT trap — can render a duration. Empty
411	# until set; readers degrade to "?s" on cache-miss (mirrors _runner_duration_token).
412	_RUNNER_PIPELINE_START_MS=""
413	
414	# ─── _runner_now_ms (#508) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
415	# Millisecond wall clock. Honors ZBUILD_STAGE_IO_NOW_MS_OVERRIDE so goldens
416	# can pin the timestamp (same env var as stage-io.sh — single test contract;
417	# do NOT introduce a runner-specific override name). Non-numeric override is
418	# treated as unset (defensive: a stray export shouldn't crash the runner).
419	# Empty stdout on failure → caller renders "??:??:?? UTC" / "?s" — no crash.
420	_runner_now_ms() {
421	    local ovr="${ZBUILD_STAGE_IO_NOW_MS_OVERRIDE:-}"
422	    if [[ -n "$ovr" && "$ovr" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
423	        printf '%s' "$ovr"
424	        return 0
425	    fi
426	    if [[ -n "${EPOCHREALTIME:-}" ]]; then
427	        local us="${EPOCHREALTIME/./}"
428	        printf '%s' $(( 10#${us} / 1000 ))
429	        return 0
430	    fi
431	    printf '%s' "$(( ${EPOCHSECONDS:-$(date -u +%s)} * 1000 ))"
432	}

434	# ─── _runner_status_comment_spawn <state_dir> <events_jsonl> <repo_root> ─────
435	# #2131 (ADR-064): the live run-status comment is a SIDECAR that tails
436	# events.jsonl — the engine never renders GitHub markdown itself, it only
437	# starts an observer and stops it. Spawned here, in the runner, so a local
438	# `zbuild pipeline start --issue N` and the CI workflow share one code path
439	# (CI needs no extra step: GITHUB_TOKEN is already job-level env). Every
440	# gate that keeps a test's temp repo off GitHub lives in rsc_enabled; the
441	# harness also pins ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT=0. The sidecar's fd 3 is closed so
442	# it never holds the stage-io channel open.
443	_RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=""
444	_runner_status_comment_spawn() {
445	    local state_dir="$1" events_jsonl="$2" repo_root="${3:-$PWD}"
446	    _RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=""
447	    # The explicit kill switch leaves NO trace — not even a log line. The
448	    # parity golden lists every file in the state dir, and every test runs
449	    # with the switch on (run-tests.sh); a "disabled" file there would be
450	    # noise in every fixture for a fact the operator already knows.
451	    [[ "${ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT:-1}" == "0" ]] && return 0
452	    local lib="$_ZBUILD_ROOT/scripts/lib/run-status-comment.sh"
453	    [[ -f "$lib" ]] || return 0
454	    # shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/run-status-comment.sh
455	    source "$lib" 2>/dev/null || return 0
456	    rsc_enabled "$state_dir" "$repo_root" || return 0
457	    local slug; slug="$(zbuild_repo_slug "$repo_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
458	    ( exec 3>&- 2>/dev/null
459	      exec bash "$lib" --events "$events_jsonl" --state-dir "$state_dir" \
460	           --parent-pid $$ --slug "$slug" --issue "${ZBUILD_ISSUE:-0}" \
461	           --run-id "${ZBUILD_RUN_ID:-}" --repo-root "$repo_root" ) \
462	        </dev/null >>"$state_dir/status-comment.log" 2>&1 &
463	    _RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=$!
464	    return 0
465	}

467	# ─── _runner_status_comment_reap ─────────────────────────────────────────────
468	# Idempotent (clears the pid first) and rc-neutral (`return 0`, every line
469	# tolerant): it runs inside the EXIT trap under `set -e`, and the process exit
470	# status must never depend on GitHub. TERM, bounded wait, KILL backstop.
471	_runner_status_comment_reap() {
472	    local pid="${_RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID:-}"
473	    [[ -n "$pid" ]] || return 0
474	    _RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=""
475	    if kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
476	        kill -TERM "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
477	        local i
478	        for (( i = 0; i < ${ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT_REAP_TIMEOUT:-45} * 10; i++ )); do
479	            kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || break
480	            sleep 0.1
481	        done
482	        kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null && kill -KILL "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
483	    fi
484	    wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
485	    return 0
486	}

488	# ─── _runner_now_short (#508) — HH:MM:SS UTC for stage banners ───────────────
489	# Returns ??:??:?? UTC when the underlying clock primitive yields nothing
490	# (defensive — the operator-visible banner still renders without crashing).
491	_runner_now_short() {
492	    local ms; ms="$(_runner_now_ms)"
493	    if [[ -z "$ms" || ! "$ms" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
494	        printf '??:??:?? UTC'
495	        return 0
496	    fi
497	    local sec=$(( ms / 1000 ))
498	    local out
499	    # The shell's clock, in UTC (ADR-065 §5); the date forms stay as the fallback.
500	    TZ=UTC printf -v out '%(%H:%M:%S UTC)T' "$sec" 2>/dev/null && [[ -n "$out" ]] && { printf '%s' "$out"; return 0; }
501	    out="$(date -u -r "$sec" +'%H:%M:%S UTC' 2>/dev/null \
502	        || date -u -d "@$sec" +'%H:%M:%S UTC' 2>/dev/null \
503	        || printf '??:??:?? UTC')"
504	    printf '%s' "$out"
505	}

507	# ─── _runner_duration_token <stage> (#508) ───────────────────────────────────
508	# Format the elapsed duration since the start cache was populated. Mirrors
509	# stage-io.sh::_stage_io_render_duration's "<N.N>s" for sub-minute durations;
510	# for >= 60 s we use "<m>m<ss>s" so a slow stage doesn't render as "127.4s".
511	# Cache miss → "?s" (no crash).
512	_runner_duration_token() {
513	    local stage="$1"
514	    local start="${_RUNNER_STAGE_START_MS[$stage]:-}"
515	    if [[ -z "$start" || ! "$start" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
516	        printf '?s'
517	        return 0
518	    fi
519	    local now; now="$(_runner_now_ms)"
520	    if [[ -z "$now" || ! "$now" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
521	        printf '?s'
522	        return 0
523	    fi
524	    local ms=$(( now - start ))
525	    (( ms < 0 )) && ms=0
526	    if (( ms < 60000 )); then
527	        awk -v m="$ms" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1fs", m/1000}'
528	    else
529	        local total_s=$(( ms / 1000 ))
530	        local mins=$(( total_s / 60 ))
531	        local secs=$(( total_s % 60 ))
532	        printf '%dm%02ds' "$mins" "$secs"
533	    fi
534	}

536	# ─── _runner_export_scope_allowlist <state_dir> (ADR-043) ────────────────────
537	# Redaction by construction: the per-run scope allowlist, exported as
538	# ZBUILD_SCOPE_ALLOWLIST so route_to_model can redact without a plugin passing
539	# it. Called per-stage because nothing is reported before plan runs (empty then —
540	# harmless, the scope manifest is the base allowlist and this is purely ADDITIVE).
541	_runner_export_scope_allowlist() {
542	    local state_dir="$1"
543	    local rec="$state_dir/artifacts/stage-reports.json" csv=""
544	    # #2189: the scope files stages REPORTED (plan reports its files) — the
545	    # engine no longer reads plan.json by path.
546	    if [[ -s "$rec" ]]; then
547	        csv="$(jq -r '(.scope_files // []) | unique | join(",")' "$rec" 2>/dev/null || echo "")"
548	    fi
549	    # #1874: the shape floor is part of the scope — computed here, mechanically,
550	    # so build, redaction and shape-floor all read one list that already holds
551	    # the files a shape change owes. Memoised per scope: this runs every stage.
552	    if [[ -n "$csv" && "$csv" != "${_RUNNER_FLOOR_KEY:-}" ]]; then
553	        _RUNNER_FLOOR_KEY="$csv"; _RUNNER_FLOOR_CSV="$csv"
554	        if ! declare -F sf_scope_floor_files >/dev/null 2>&1; then
555	            # shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/shape-floor.sh
556	            source "${_ZBUILD_CONTRACT_LIB_DIR:-$_ZBUILD_ROOT/scripts/lib}/shape-floor.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
557	        fi
558	        if declare -F sf_scope_floor_files >/dev/null 2>&1; then

570	# ─── _runner_record_report <state_dir> <stage> <report-json> (#2189) ─────────
571	# Merge one dispatch's report into the run's record, artifacts/stage-reports.json
572	# (under artifacts/ so it is snapshotted and restored with the run): scope and
573	# wiring files are unioned; owned files are kept per reporting stage, so the
574	# deny list can exempt the owner. Engine setup reads THIS record — never a
575	# stage's artifact by name. Best-effort: a failed merge leaves the prior record.
576	# Parallel members record concurrently, so the read-merge-write holds a mkdir
577	# lock (portable; flock is absent on stock macOS) — else a sibling's merge is lost.
578	# A lock left by a killed holder is reclaimed after 10s.
579	_runner_record_report() {
580	    local state_dir="$1" stage="$2" report="${3:-}"
581	    [[ -n "$state_dir" && -n "$stage" && -n "$report" && "$report" != "{}" ]] || return 0
582	    # Most stages report none of the setup fields — skip the lock and the jq fork.
583	    [[ "$report" == *'"scope_files"'* || "$report" == *'"owned_files"'* \
584	        || "$report" == *'"wiring_files"'* ]] || return 0
585	    local rec="$state_dir/artifacts/stage-reports.json" tmp
586	    local lock="$state_dir/.stage-reports.lock" _tries=0
587	    [[ -d "$state_dir/artifacts" ]] || mkdir -p "$state_dir/artifacts" 2>/dev/null || return 0
588	    until mkdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null; do
589	        # A merge takes milliseconds; a lock held 10s belongs to a dead holder.
590	        if (( ++_tries > 200 )); then rmdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null; _tries=0; fi
591	        sleep 0.05
592	    done
593	    [[ -s "$rec" ]] || printf '{}' > "$rec"
594	    tmp="$rec.tmp.$BASHPID"
595	    if jq --arg s "$stage" --argjson r "$report" '
596	            .scope_files  = ((.scope_files  // []) + ($r.scope_files  // []) | unique)
597	          | .wiring_files = ((.wiring_files // []) + ($r.wiring_files // []) | unique)
598	          | if ($r.owned_files // null) != null
599	              then .owned_files = ((.owned_files // {}) + {($s): ($r.owned_files | unique)})
600	              else . end' "$rec" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
601	        mv -f "$tmp" "$rec"
602	    else
603	        rm -f "$tmp"
604	    fi
605	    rmdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null
606	    return 0
607	}

609	# ─── _runner_validate_leaf_resolvability <stages_arr_name> <plugins_root> ─────
610	# ADR-047 §5: the manifest-derived membership fence — the sole membership
611	# enforcement (the old hardcoded-roster fence is deleted, #1299). Every leaf in the
612	# resolved template flow must resolve to a plugin via resolve_stage_plugin
613	# (role-then-id, ADR-042); an unresolved leaf names the id.
614	#
615	# It is a CONTRACT check, so it is gated by the SAME ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR mode
616	# the inter-stage contract-validator uses (they must agree). Load-time membership
617	# enforcement is the ENFORCE-mode job; the opt-out modes (warn/off) skip it — so
618	# this preflight is a TRUE NO-OP whenever enforcement is off and never perturbs the
619	# mock-roster suites that drive runner.sh under warn (they resolve their leaves at
620	# dispatch via mocked plugin_hook_call, not through a real registry):
621	#   - enforce (default, real runs) / unset → ERROR fail-closed (rc=2). This is the
622	#     load-time guarantee that replaces the old canonical membership gate.
623	#   - warn / off (or any unknown mode)     → skip. Dispatch-time resolution
624	#     (resolve_stage_plugin in the stage loop) still fails a genuinely-missing
625	#     plugin mid-run — the backstop for opt-out runs.
626	# Takes the stage array BY NAME to avoid a subshell copy on read.
627	_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability() {
628	    local _arr_name="$1" plugins_root="$2"
629	    # Only enforce gates at load; warn/off/unknown are opt-outs → no-op. (The
630	    # default is enforce, matching contract-validator's default; unknown modes
631	    # degrade to non-enforce, exactly as contract-validator degrades them to warn.)
632	    [[ "${ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR:-enforce}" == "enforce" ]] || return 0
633	    # Validate the array name is a plain identifier before binding the nameref
634	    # below — never bind a name assembled from unvalidated input (Copilot #1290:
635	    # injection footgun). Callers pass a literal ("active_stages"), so a
636	    # non-identifier is a programming error, not runtime data.
637	    if [[ ! "$_arr_name" =~ ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ ]]; then
638	        error "_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: invalid array name '${_arr_name}'"
639	        return 1
640	    fi
641	    # bash errors on a nameref that resolves to itself; reject it with our own
642	    # message rather than a raw "circular name reference" from the shell.
643	    if [[ "$_arr_name" == "_stages" ]]; then
644	        error "_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: array name '_stages' collides with the nameref"
645	        return 1
646	    fi
647	    # Warm the manifest cache in THIS shell before resolving anything. Every
648	    # resolution below reads manifests through `$( )`, and an associative-array
649	    # write inside a command substitution dies with that subshell — so a lazily
650	    # filled cache is never inherited (#1614, the reason yaml_cache_prewarm
651	    # exists and main() calls it at line ~1370).
652	    #
653	    # main() is not the only entry point. Tests source this file and call helpers
654	    # directly, never reaching that prewarm, and then every lookup forks awk:
655	    # template-resolvability-preflight-test.sh made 28,068 yaml_get calls with
656	    # ZERO cache hits, at real 150s / user 52s / sys 81s — kernel time 1.55x
657	    # user, which is process creation, not computation. Prewarming here took it
658	    # to 82.75s with sys 81s -> 45s.
659	    #
660	    # Here and not in setup_test_env: the prewarm costs 1.32s, and 570 test
661	    # files would pay ~747s for it to benefit the few that resolve plugins.
662	    # Measured before choosing the seam.
663	    #
664	    # Idempotent: a second call re-reads the same keys, which are now cache
665	    # hits. Cheap no-op in production, where main() has already warmed it.
666	    if declare -F yaml_cache_prewarm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
667	        yaml_cache_prewarm "$plugins_root"
668	    fi
669	    # Discovery too, for the same reason and in the same shell: it validates
670	    # every manifest on every call (~1.47s even with the yaml cache warm) and
671	    # runs once per leaf. 19 leaves x 2 templates was 38 full re-validations of
672	    # an unchanged tree.
673	    if declare -F discover_plugins >/dev/null 2>&1; then
674	        discover_plugins "$plugins_root" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
675	    fi
676	    local -n _stages="${_arr_name}"
677	    local _leaf _ok=1
678	    for _leaf in "${_stages[@]+"${_stages[@]}"}"; do
679	        [[ -z "$_leaf" ]] && continue
680	        # A cycle/parallel GROUP id is a composition operator, not a leaf, and is
681	        # not itself a plugin — its members are already flattened into the stage
682	        # list. Skip group ids (their _TPL_STAGE_TYPE_<id> is cycle|parallel).
683	        local _t_var="_TPL_STAGE_TYPE_${_leaf//-/_}"
684	        case "${!_t_var:-leaf}" in
685	            cycle|parallel) continue ;;
686	        esac
687	        if ! resolve_stage_plugin "$_leaf" "$plugins_root" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
688	            error "load_template: stage '${_leaf}' resolves to no plugin (ADR-047 §5: every leaf must resolve via role or id; add a plugin whose provides.role matches, or whose id is '${_leaf}')"
689	            _ok=0
690	        fi
691	    done
692	    [[ $_ok -eq 1 ]]
693	}

695	# ─── _runner_validate_startup_preflight [violation_fixture] (ADR-051 §warn-first) ──
696	# Aggregation SKELETON (#1318 / D1): owns the violations[]/fail_count collection,
697	# the render-all-at-once block (same pattern as _contract_validate_pipeline) and the
698	# warn/enforce/off mode dispatch. Separate gate from _runner_validate_leaf_
699	# resolvability — it covers non-contract elements the DAG validator does not address.
700	#
701	# It deliberately contributes NO checks of its own yet. The concrete producers land
702	# downstream, each against the discriminating fixtures #1605 pre-stages:
703	#   - persona-binding existence (PERSONA_MISSING) → #1320 (D3)
704	#   - requires.plugins resolution (PLUGIN_MISSING) → #1321 (D4)
705	# An earlier draft carried both checks here, untested; the requires.plugins one was
706	# an acknowledged approximation that raised spurious PLUGIN_MISSING for any entry
707	# naming an ordinary plugin. Shipping checks no test discriminates is the green-but-
708	# inert shape #1605 exists to prevent, so they were removed rather than carried.
709	#
710	# Deliberate divergence from _runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: the DEFAULT mode
711	# here is WARN (not enforce). This lands warn-first so operators see failures before
712	# enforcement is mandatory. Set ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=enforce to fail-closed.
713	# ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=off is a full no-op (skips all checks, emits nothing).
714	#
715	# The optional first argument is a synthetic violation fixture: it injects one
716	# pre-formed violation so the aggregation, rendering and mode dispatch are testable
717	# before any real producer exists. A non-empty string yields exactly one violation;
718	# empty (or omitted) yields none. Runtime call sites in runner.sh pass no argument,
719	# so until D3/D4 land the live path always renders nothing and returns 0.
720	# _runner_template_personas <template> — every persona the template names, one
721	# "<where>|<persona id>" per line: <where> is the section, or section/element
722	# for a map element's own persona (ADR-051 §2).
723	_runner_template_personas() {
724	    awk '
725	        function indent(s,   i) { i = 0; while (substr(s, i+1, 1) == " ") i++; return i }
726	        /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
727	        /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*:/ { sec = $0; sub(/:.*/, "", sec); el = ""; els_ind = -1; next }
728	        /^[[:space:]]+elements:[[:space:]]*$/ { els_ind = indent($0); next }
729	        els_ind >= 0 && /[^[:space:]]/ && indent($0) <= els_ind { els_ind = -1; el = "" }
730	        els_ind >= 0 && /^[[:space:]]+-[[:space:]]/ {
731	            el = $0; sub(/^[[:space:]]+-[[:space:]]+/, "", el); sub(/^id:[[:space:]]*/, "", el)
732	            sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, "", el); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, "", el); next
733	        }
734	        /^[[:space:]]+persona:[[:space:]]*[^[:space:]#]/ {
735	            id = $0; sub(/^[[:space:]]+persona:[[:space:]]*/, "", id); sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, "", id)
736	            gsub(/[[:space:]"\047]/, "", id)
737	            print (el != "" ? sec "/" el : sec) "|" id
738	        }
739	    ' "$1" 2>/dev/null
740	}

917	# startup in _RUNNER_ERR_FD (ADR-054 §7). A trap that fires inside a call made

919	# /dev/null when SIGTERM landed during one. A no-op when nothing was saved.

925	_render_pipeline_end() {
926	    local status="${1:-unknown}"
927	    local stage_hint="${2:-}"
928	    local rc_hint="${3:-}"
929	    local run_id="${_runner_run_id:-?}"
930	    local issue="${_runner_issue:-?}"
931	    # Best-effort value gathering. Each `$(...)` here forks a helper that may
932	    # itself fork an external (awk in the duration token, date/tput in the
933	    # clock/width helpers). Most call sites invoke this banner DIRECTLY under the
934	    # runner's `set -e` (e.g. the cycle/stage abort + LLM/scope-abort paths) —
935	    # not wrapped in `|| true` — so a transient under-load fork failure in any
936	    # one of these bare assignments would trip errexit and abort the render
937	    # BEFORE the printf block, silently dropping the operator's terminal banner
938	    # mid-teardown. `|| fallback` neutralizes errexit at each assignment so the
939	    # banner is always emitted once the function is reached, on every call site.
940	    # (#1156)
941	    local dur; dur="$(_runner_pipeline_duration_token)" || dur='?s'
942	    local glyph; glyph="$(_pipeline_status_glyph "$status")" || glyph='✗'
943	    local color; color="$(_pipeline_status_color "$status")" || color=''
944	    local frame="${BLUE:-}"
945	    local ts; ts="$(_runner_now_short)" || ts='??:??:?? UTC'

948	    # Map status → operator-friendly verb for line 2. Tracks event payload
949	    # verbatim so "status=<X>" agrees with the verb. ("success" in legacy
950	    # event payloads renders as "complete" — see ADR-015 §v5 amendment).
951	    local word
952	    case "$status" in
953	        success|complete)        word="complete" ;;
954	        complete_unconverged)    word="complete_unconverged" ;;
955	        failed)                  word="failed" ;;
956	        interrupted)             word="interrupted" ;;
957	        aborted)                 word="aborted" ;;
958	        preflight_failed)        word="preflight_failed" ;;
959	        *)                       word="$status" ;;
960	    esac
961	
962	    local label=" pipeline.end "
963	    # Layout: <left_bar><label><mid_bar> <ts>
964	    local left_bar=$(( (width - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1) / 2 ))
965	    local mid_bar=$(( width - left_bar - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1 ))
966	
967	    local detail_status="status=${status}"
968	    [[ -n "$stage_hint" ]] && detail_status+=" stage=${stage_hint}"
969	    [[ -n "$rc_hint"    ]] && detail_status+=" rc=${rc_hint}"
970	
971	    if [[ "$mid_bar" -le 2 ]]; then
972	        # Degraded layout — drop timestamp from the header.
973	        local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
974	        [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
975	        local bar
976	        printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
977	        bar="${bar// /═}"
978	        {
979	            printf '\n'
980	            printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' "$frame" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" "$frame" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
981	            printf '%b%b%s%b Pipeline %s: %s run_id=%s issue=%s (took %s)\n' \
982	                "$color" "${BOLD:-}" "$glyph" "${RESET:-}" \
983	                "$word" "$detail_status" "$run_id" "$issue" "$dur"
984	        } >&2
985	        _runner_render_open_items "$status" || true
986	        return 0
987	    fi
988	
989	    local lbar rbar
990	    printf -v lbar '%*s' "$left_bar" ''; lbar="${lbar// /═}"
991	    printf -v rbar '%*s' "$mid_bar"  ''; rbar="${rbar// /═}"
992	    {
993	        printf '\n'
994	        printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b %s\n' \
995	            "$frame" "$lbar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
996	            "$frame" "$rbar" "${RESET:-}" "$ts"
997	        printf '%b%b%s%b Pipeline %s: %s run_id=%s issue=%s (took %s)\n' \
998	            "$color" "${BOLD:-}" "$glyph" "${RESET:-}" \
999	            "$word" "$detail_status" "$run_id" "$issue" "$dur"
1000	    } >&2
1001	    _runner_render_open_items "$status" || true
1002	}
1003	
1004	# _runner_render_open_items <status> — #2330 (ADR-068 §8): a run that did not
1005	# pass ends by saying why in words and naming each open item, with what would
1006	# settle it. pipeline.end keeps the engine's code; this is what a reader sees.
1007	_runner_render_open_items() {
1008	    case "${1:-}" in failed|interrupted|aborted) ;; *) return 0 ;; esac
1009	    [[ -n "${_runner_state_file:-}" ]] && declare -F open_items_markdown >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
1010	    local sd="${_runner_state_file%/*}" items n
1011	    items="$(open_items_markdown "$sd")" || items=""
1012	    n=0; [[ -n "$items" ]] && n="$(grep -c '^[0-9][0-9]*\. ' <<< "$items" || true)"
1013	    {
1014	        printf 'The run %s.\n' "$(run_end_words "${_CYCLE_LAST_TERMINATED_REASON:-}" "$n")"
1015	        [[ -n "$items" ]] && printf '%s\n' "$items"
1016	    } >&2
1017	}
1018	
1019	# ─── _render_stage_divider <stage> (#492, ts: #508) ──────────────────────────
1020	# Emits a blank line + a heavy horizontal rule (━ U+2501) with the stage name
1021	# centered in stage-color, then another blank line — written to fd 2 so it
1022	# survives the same redirection rules as ▸/✓/✗ info lines. Used on every
1023	# stage transition (between eb_emit_event "stage.start" and "▸ Running stage")
1024	# so the operator's eye finds the next stage boundary at a glance.
1025	#
1026	# #508: right-align an HH:MM:SS UTC timestamp on the divider, mirroring the
1027	# stage-io banner header right-alignment (_stage_io_compose_banner). Width
1028	# math (no bookend glyphs in this layout — just bars + label + sep + ts):
1029	#   visible = left_bar + len(label) + mid_bar + 1 (space) + len(ts)
1030	#   left_bar = (width - len(label) - len(ts) - 1) / 2
1031	#   mid_bar  = width - left_bar - len(label) - len(ts) - 1
1032	# Degrade rule: when mid_bar <= 2 (very narrow terminals) we drop the
1033	# timestamp and emit the legacy symmetric divider so layout stays legible.
1034	_render_stage_divider() {
1035	    local stage="$1"
1036	    local width
1037	    width="$(_term_width)"
1038	    local color
1039	    color="$(_stage_color "$stage")"
1040	    local label=" ${stage} "
1041	    local ts; ts="$(_runner_now_short)"
1042	
1043	    # Layout: <left_bar><label><mid_bar> <ts>
1044	    # Visible width = left_bar + len(label) + mid_bar + 1 (sep) + len(ts).
1045	    local left_bar=$(( (width - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1) / 2 ))
1046	    local mid_bar=$(( width - left_bar - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1 ))
1047	
1048	    if [[ "$mid_bar" -le 2 ]]; then
1049	        # Degraded: legacy symmetric divider, no timestamp (narrow terminal).
1050	        local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
1051	        [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
1052	        local bar
1053	        printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
1054	        bar="${bar// /━}"
1055	        {
1056	            printf '\n'
1057	            printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' "$color" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" "$color" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
1058	            printf '\n'
1059	            # #523: trailing blank line — combined with the existing leading
1060	            # \n above, produces two stacked blanks between consecutive stages.
1061	            # Cycle sub-dividers (ADR-015 §v6) intentionally do NOT add this.
1062	            printf '\n'
1063	        } >&2
1064	        return 0
1065	    fi
1066	
1067	    local lbar rbar
1068	    printf -v lbar '%*s' "$left_bar" ''; lbar="${lbar// /━}"
1069	    printf -v rbar '%*s' "$mid_bar"  ''; rbar="${rbar// /━}"
1070	    {
1071	        printf '\n'
1072	        # %b on colored fragments so \033[...] resolves like echo -e elsewhere.
1073	        # Timestamp is plain text outside color escapes — NO_COLOR keeps it.
1074	        printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b %s\n' \
1075	            "$color" "$lbar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
1076	            "$color" "$rbar" "${RESET:-}" "$ts"
1077	        printf '\n'
1078	        # #523: trailing blank line — combined with the leading \n above,
1079	        # produces two stacked blanks between consecutive stages. Cycle
1080	        # sub-dividers (ADR-015 §v6) intentionally do NOT add this.
1081	        printf '\n'
1082	    } >&2
1083	}
1084	
1085	# ─── Cycle banner helpers (#524, ADR-015 §v6, ADR-021) ───────────────────────
1086	# Operator-fd-2 chrome for outer cycles (ADR-021). These render a visual
1087	# hierarchy that nests cleanly with the existing stage-transition divider
1088	# (_render_stage_divider) so the operator can see cycle entry, per-iter
1089	# boundaries, per-iter outcomes, and cycle exit in the scrollback.
1090	#
1091	# Glyph + color ladder (heaviest → lightest):
1092	#   ━━━ (U+2501) stage transition   — BOLD BLUE (handled in _render_stage_divider)
1093	#   ═══ (U+2550) cycle entry/exit   — LIGHT_BLUE
1094	#   ─── (U+2500) cycle iter divider — CYAN
1095	#
1096	# Routing contract (silent-failure mitigations):
1097	#   - All 4 helpers write to fd 2 ONLY. Hardcoded `>&2`. NEVER capture in $(…)
1098	#     — output would vanish. Banner emit follows event emit (event=durable,
1099	#     banner=best-effort).
1100	#   - `{ ...; } >&2 2>/dev/null || true` is used so a broken stderr can never
1101	#     abort the cycle. Each block is a single printf wrapped in the redirect
1102	#     group so SIGINT during banner emit cannot race on partial writes.
1103	#   - These banners are fd-2 ONLY and NEVER appear in the PR comment body
1104	#     rendered by gh_comment. Operator chrome only.
1105	#
1106	# Determinism: honors ZBUILD_TERM_WIDTH_OVERRIDE + ZBUILD_STAGE_IO_NOW_MS_OVERRIDE
1107	# via _term_width / _runner_now_short (same contract as _render_stage_divider).
1108	
1109	# ─── _render_cycle_entry <cycle_id> <max> <stages_csv> ───────────────────────
1110	# Heavy `═` LIGHT_BLUE divider + `▸ Entering cycle <id>` line + DIM trailer
1111	# (max + stages). Emitted by the runner BEFORE cycle_orchestrator_run so the
1112	# operator's eye finds the cycle boundary before the first iter divider.
1113	_render_cycle_entry() {
1114	    local cycle_id="$1" max="$2" stages_csv="${3:-}" description="${4:-}"
1115	    local width; width="$(_term_width)"
1116	    local label=" cycle: ${cycle_id} "
1117	    local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
1118	    [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
1119	    local bar
1120	    printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
1121	    bar="${bar// /═}"
1122	    {
1123	        printf '\n'
1124	        printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' \
1125	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
1126	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
1127	        printf '%b%b▸%b Entering cycle: %b%b%s%b\n' \
1128	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "${BOLD:-}" "${RESET:-}" \
1129	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "${BOLD:-}" "$cycle_id" "${RESET:-}"
1130	        # #831: operator-facing description on its own DIM line, between the
1131	        # Entering-cycle headline and the (max_iterations=…) trailer. Skipped
1132	        # entirely when description is empty so templates without it render
1133	        # identically to the pre-#831 banner (golden tests stay valid).
1134	        if [[ -n "$description" ]]; then
1135	            printf '%b  %s%b\n' "${DIM:-}" "$description" "${RESET:-}"
1136	        fi
1137	        printf '%b  (max_iterations=%s · stages=%s)%b\n' \
1138	            "${DIM:-}" "$max" "$stages_csv" "${RESET:-}"
1139	        printf '\n'
1140	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1141	}
1142	
1143	# ─── _render_parallel_entry <group_id> <max_parallel> <members_csv> ──────────
1144	# ADR-039 (#1131): clone of _render_cycle_entry for a parallel stage group.
1145	# Heavy `═` LIGHT_BLUE divider + `▸ Entering parallel group <id>` line + DIM
1146	# trailer (max_parallel + members). Emitted by the runner BEFORE
1147	# parallel_group_run so the operator's eye finds the group boundary first.
1148	_render_parallel_entry() {
1149	    local group_id="$1" max="$2" members_csv="${3:-}"
1150	    local width; width="$(_term_width)"
1151	    local label=" parallel: ${group_id} "
1152	    local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
1153	    [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
1154	    local bar
1155	    printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
1156	    bar="${bar// /═}"
1157	    {
1158	        printf '\n'
1159	        printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' \
1160	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
1161	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
1162	        printf '%b%b▸%b Entering parallel group: %b%b%s%b\n' \
1163	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "${BOLD:-}" "${RESET:-}" \
1164	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "${BOLD:-}" "$group_id" "${RESET:-}"
1165	        printf '%b  (max_parallel=%s · members=%s)%b\n' \
1166	            "${DIM:-}" "$max" "$members_csv" "${RESET:-}"
1167	        printf '\n'
1168	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1169	}
1170	
1171	# ─── _render_parallel_group_complete <group_id> <member_count> <failure_count> ─
1172	# Issue OUT (ADR-039): DIM trailer after a parallel group's per-member lines,
1173	# mirroring _render_cycle_exit's role for cycles. e.g.
1174	# `▸ review_lenses complete — 5 members, 0 blocking`.
1175	_render_parallel_group_complete() {
1176	    local group_id="$1" count="${2:-0}" fail="${3:-0}"
1177	    {
1178	        printf '%b▸ %s complete — %s members, %s blocking%b\n' \
1179	            "${DIM:-}" "$group_id" "$count" "$fail" "${RESET:-}"
1180	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1181	}
1182	
1183	# ─── _render_cycle_iter_divider <cycle_id> <iter> <max> ───────────────────────
1184	# Light `─` CYAN sub-divider for each iter boundary, e.g.
1185	# `─── build_test_cycle iter 2/5 ─────`. When this cycle is nested inside
1186	# another cycle the orchestrator has already set ZBUILD_SEQ_PREFIX (e.g.
1187	# `4.1`) — surface it as a `[<prefix>]` prefix so operators can tell at a
1188	# glance which outer iter this divider belongs to:
1189	#   outer (no prefix): `─── build_review_cycle iter 1/2 ───`
1190	#   inner (prefix set): `─── [4.1] build_test_cycle iter 1/3 ───`
1191	# Reuses the seq-prefix machinery from Wave 19-B #718 / cycle-orchestrator.sh:888
1192	# — no new plumbing, no hook-signature change. Emitted by the orchestrator's
1193	# iter-begin hook BEFORE the first per-stage banner of the iter.
1194	_render_cycle_iter_divider() {
1195	    local cycle_id="$1" iter="$2" max="$3"
1196	    local prefix="${ZBUILD_SEQ_PREFIX:-}"
1197	    local label
1198	    if [[ -n "$prefix" ]]; then
1199	        label=" [${prefix}] ${cycle_id} iter ${iter}/${max} "
1200	    else
1201	        label=" ${cycle_id} iter ${iter}/${max} "
1202	    fi
1203	    local width; width="$(_term_width)"
1204	    local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
1205	    [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
1206	    local bar
1207	    printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
1208	    bar="${bar// /─}"
1209	    {
1210	        printf '\n%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' \
1211	            "${CYAN:-}" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
1212	            "${CYAN:-}" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
1213	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1214	}
1215	
1216	# ─── _render_cycle_iter_complete <iter> <verdict> <score> <fc> <elapsed_s> ──
1217	# Per-iter DIM trailer line e.g. `↳ iter 2 complete: verdict=pass score=-1
1218	# failure_count=1 elapsed=4s`. Emitted by the orchestrator's iter-complete
1219	# hook AFTER the `cycle.iteration.complete` event is durable. #1254: the
1220	# `score` axis (progress − defects) replaced the retired `velocity` label so
1221	# the per-iter line matches the OUTPUT banner's health score.
1222	_render_cycle_iter_complete() {
1223	    local iter="$1" verdict="$2" score="$3" failure_count="$4" elapsed_s="$5"
1224	    {
1225	        printf '%b↳ iter %s complete: verdict=%s score=%s failure_count=%s elapsed=%ss%b\n' \
1226	            "${DIM:-}" "$iter" "$verdict" "$score" "$failure_count" "$elapsed_s" "${RESET:-}"
1227	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1228	}
1229
